fieldNotes.author: Site maintainer
fieldNotes.body:
Confirmed on the ground: a baseball/soccer field, basketball courts, a gaga pit, the playground, shade, paved paths, trails and charcoal grills. Three of those were sitting at "Not confirmed" — courts and fields, paved paths, and grills.

The gaga pit has no field and isn't getting one. A schema field for something one park in nineteen has would print "Not confirmed" on the other eighteen, which is noise pretending to be rigour. It lives here, where somebody with a nine-year-old will find it.

blurb: A hundred-acre du Pont estate garden given to the city in 1942, sitting outside the city limits near Hoopes Reservoir. A paved path along a creek, and in early spring the magnolias and the daffodil bank. That's genuinely it — no playground, no pavilion, no plumbing. Come for a walk and the flowering trees, not for an afternoon.

restrooms.note: A portable unit. Not a plumbed block — the city's amenity list doesn't mention restrooms at all, so this is only here because someone stood in front of it.

hoursNote: The city publishes no hours for this park.
warnings: Outside Wilmington city limits despite being a city park. It's in Greenville.

name: Can-Do Playground
blurb: The state's big accessible playground, inside Alapocas Run State Park. Ramps to the upper decks rather than steps, poured rubber under the swings, shade over the main structure, and sand tables raised high enough to pull a wheelchair under. A Ninja Fit obstacle course and a picnic pavilion sit in the same field.

restrooms.note: Between the Can-Do Playground and the Ninja Fit course, and well kept. Confirmed in person.

accessibility: Ramps to most of the upper decks rather than steps only, poured rubber under the swings, concrete paths right up to the equipment, and raised sand tables. Confirmed in person August 2026.
hoursNote: First-hand, 8 August 2026. Covers the whole day-use area — the park, the Can-Do Playground and the Ninja Fit course all keep the same hours.
warnings: NO DOGS. The sign at the entrance reads "No pets allowed in playground area", and the park's own board lists pets among the things prohibited. Service animals are named as welcome. You can walk the dog on the greenway; you cannot bring it in here.
This is inside a state park, not a county or town park. It appears here because it is a playground and that is how people look for it.
outstanding: Which parking lot is nearest — the park map shows C and D beside it.
Does the pet ban cover the whole day-use field or only inside the fence?
Any age split on the equipment, and is the Ninja Fit course age-limited?
Are the restrooms open year-round, or seasonal?

photos.alt: A wide view of a large playground with brown ramps and railings up to elevated decks, a shade canopy over the center, wood-chip surfacing and concrete paths.

photos.alt: A green-roofed timber picnic pavilion with picnic tables under it, on grass beside a paved path, with the ninja course visible in the distance behind.

photos.caption: The sign that decides whether the dog gets out of the car.

photos.alt: A sign reading NINJA FIT PLAY GROUND in white on black, with cartoon ninja characters, standing at the end of a curved black warped wall on mown grass.
photos.caption: The sign at the end of the run. Built with Rotary and the Neighborhood Ninjas; the warped wall in front of it is the last obstacle.

photos.alt: A long outdoor ninja obstacle course on black rubber surfacing: balance beams, angled boards, hanging rings and climbing frames, with two children on it and open playing fields either side.
photos.caption: The whole run, looking down it. Rubber underfoot the entire length, and benches along the edge for whoever isn't doing it.

photos.alt: Two tall angled climbing boards with green hand-holds in the foreground of a ninja obstacle course, with monkey bars and balance equipment behind and a child in the middle distance.
photos.caption: The climbing boards, from inside the course. This end is the harder half — the balance and hanging obstacles are down the other.

photos.alt: A wide view across mown grass to a long ninja obstacle course silhouetted against a bright sky, with a small child walking towards it.
photos.caption: How it sits in the field. It's a long walk across open grass from the parking, and there is no shade on the course itself.

fieldNotes.author: Site maintainer
fieldNotes.body: The Ninja Fit course has four photographs of its own now, including the sign. It had none — and worse, the file I had labeled `cando-ninja` and captioned as the course is a photograph of the picnic pavilion, with the course a thin dark line on the horizon behind it. I named it wrong and then wrote a caption that made the wrong name true. It's `cando-pavilion` now and says what it is.

fieldNotes.author: Site maintainer
fieldNotes.body: 8am to sunset, daily — the same hours as Alapocas Run around it, and the Ninja Fit course keeps them too. New Castle County publishes nothing for this playground; the hours came from being there.
